To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ELT is dependent on the total calcium ion concentration of the reaction medium, that thrombin preparations with equal calcium ion concentrations yield comparable results of the ELT, and that the ELT of various thrombin concentrations is dependent on the calcium ion concentration.
the ELT is significantly influenced by the total calcium concentration in the reaction mixture and that this influence is different for different thrombin preparations.
the euglobin lysis time (EGL) is dependent on the total calcium content of the reaction mixture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of the calcium ion concentration of thrombin solutions and with the influence of the total calcium ion concentration of the reaction mixtures on the ELT.
the influence of the calcium ion concentration of the reaction medium on the time course of fibrin polymerisation in the presence of thrombin.
the importance of the calcium ion concentration for the euglobulins lysis time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the euglobulins are not lysed by the thrombin alone but by the thrombin-calcium complex.
the euglobulins are not only activated by thrombin but also by the Ca2+-thrombin complex.
the ELT is a function of the calcium ion concentration in the reaction mixture, and not of the thrombin activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the euglobulins are not lysed directly by the thrombin, but that a complex of calcium ions and thrombin is necessary for the lysis of the euglogulins.
the ELT is dependent on the total calcium ion concentration of the reaction medium and that a standardization of this parameter should be performed.
in the plasma the calcium ions are involved in the activation of the eugolobulin lysis and in the fibrinolysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
calcium ions are essential for the euglobulins to be converted into the fibrinogen-like fibrin monomer, but the calcium ions are not required for the fibrinogen to be converted into fibrin.
the calcium ion concentration of the thrombin solution should be standardized.
the ELT is dependent on the concentration of calcium ions.
